description: The objective-6 benchmark built to be checkable: five asynchronous masters, generated clocks at ratios 2/4/8, crossings between all five, an FSM -- and no multipliers anywhere, so a bounded equivalence check can actually close. soc_bench meets the same structural requirements and cannot be certified; cell count was never the problem, multipliers were.

known_bottlenecks: rx: bit-serial CRC32 shift, 8 dependent XOR/mux stages per byte, where a parallel update over the whole byte is the fix
parse: 96-way priority select written as a serial mux cascade, so bit 95 waits on all 95 below it
look: 256-entry CAM whose hit index resolves through a serial priority cascade over the match vector
xfrm: 512-bit parity as a serial XOR chain, depth 512 instead of 9
tx: serial accumulate over 16 terms instead of a balanced adder tree
notes.invariants: rewrites must preserve each domain's latency exactly and be bit-exact. The five datapaths share no signal except through the cdc_ synchronisers, and may be rewritten independently.
notes.cdc_off_limits: cdc_* and clk_*_div* -- enforced by tools/protect.py before synthesis. See docs/equivalence-contract.md.
notes.no_multipliers: deliberate. A bounded check unrolls the design once per solver step, and unpipelined multipliers make that intractable -- measured on soc_bench, where a bad candidate is refuted in 21 s but a good one times out at 1800 s or is OOM-killed.
notes.purpose: objective 6, in the form where the loop can both reject and promote.
